newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA MINISTERS 'FAVOURABLE' TO DEFENCE REVIEW.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA MINISTERS 'FAVOURABLE' TO DEFENCE REVIEW.

text.p: Deputy Defence Minister Ronnie Kasrils said on Wednesday cabinet colleagues had expressed support for a review of South Africa's defence needs which could pave the way for the purchase of corvettes and submarines.
"It's going well... The defence review was very favourably received," Kasrils told Reuters after a meeting of most cabinet members excluding President Nelson Mandela and Deputy President Thabo Mbeki.

The formal defence budget for 1997/98 makes no provision for the purchase of vessels to beef up South Africa's ageing navy fleet, but Kasrils and Defence Minister Joe Modise believe the money will be found if the defence review is approved by cabinet and parliament.
The review was ordered by parliament more than a year ago to assess various aspects of defence policy.

A statement issued by cabinet secretary Jakes Gerwel after the ministerial meeting on Wednesday said policy proposals on defence posture, functions, design and personnel requirements had been well received.
Modise has asked Mbeki to intervene in a dispute with Finance Minister Trevor Manuel over military funding. The defence minister has said Manuel's defence allocation is emasculating the armed forces.
Shipyards in Britain, Spain, Germany and France are keen to win any contract for additional vessels including four corvettes and possibly a number of submarines.
